minutes.headline: Planning Board approved stormwater permits for 680 Reservoir Road and 319 Highland Street, each with added conditions.
minutes.summary: The board interviewed a prospective member, then held two stormwater permit hearings for single-family homes and approved both with conditions. The Highland Street hearing drew long debate over town drainage discharging onto private property. The board also marked up the Master Plan RFP and heard committee reports and director's items.

public_comment.topic: Call for public comment at start; none given.
Caller said he was on the line but missed the chance to comment before the hearing closed; worried the project could come back to haunt the town, asked about recording maintenance on deeds.
Drainage on Highland Street is getting worse; asked whether the town should fix the pre-existing problem and what effect there would be on neighbors; questioned pipe size.
Abutter concerned about flooding of his basement and a sump pump if drainage changes; surprised the culvert is private.
Final call for public comment; none.

Approve stormwater permit for 319 Highland Street with standard conditions plus keeping the culvert opening on their property clear.
Approve minutes of November 14, 2022 meeting and the 260 Faluga Road public hearing.

budget_items.what_was_said: The RFP budget was referenced as a paid-and-done cost that would yield a deliverable; hoped it would draw responses.
The DPW director is to log staff time on stormwater work to estimate annual capital outlay for a dedicated sustainable funding mechanism.

decisions.decision: Prospective member to appear at a joint meeting with the Select Board the following Tuesday for joint appointment.
Master Plan RFP language to be revised to call for a holistic public participation structure with varied advertising and activities.
RFP deliverable to say Microsoft-compatible version plus hyperlinked PDF; history section to be edited and sent to the assistant town manager.
Driveways and entrances item tabled until the board has more members.
Joint meeting with Select Board set for next Tuesday, around 7:30, with Zoom option.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved a stormwater permit for 680 Reservoir Road by voice vote, with trash racks on both ends of the pipe and clearing limited to the driveway area.
The board approved a stormwater permit for 319 Highland Street by voice vote, with a condition to keep the culvert opening on the applicant's property clear.
The Highland Street hearing included long debate and abutter comment about town drainage discharging onto private property and a culvert that turned out to be private.
The board agreed to revise the Master Plan RFP to call for a broader public participation structure, and to table the driveways and entrances item until it has more members.
A prospective member was interviewed, and a joint meeting with the Select Board was set for the following Tuesday to make the joint appointment.

why_it_matters: Highland Street shows how drainage built by the town can end up on private land, leaving a homeowner to keep a culvert clear and nobody clearly responsible for the pre-existing problem.
The stormwater task force's staff-time logging is meant to estimate a dedicated funding mechanism, which could become a charge or budget request residents are asked to support.
The Master Plan RFP sets how much residents get to take part in the town's planning for the coming years.
watch_next: Joint meeting of the Planning Board and Select Board the following Tuesday, around 7:30 with a Zoom option, to appoint the new member.
The revised Master Plan RFP, and the DPW director's log of stormwater staff time for estimating annual capital outlay.
